summary: Module 4 REFLECT. Debugging with tools instead of code reading changed the investigation order: profiling ran BEFORE reading source, and the runtime output (tracemalloc top allocations, SQL statement counts, latency-scaling curve) decided what to look at. The fork was already hardened for the canonical leaks (get_db closes in finally; /links fires 3 statements not 51), so the tool data redirected me to the genuinely present issues: the cache module's acquire-without-guaranteed-release pattern (fixed with finally), and the unbounded long_url input that made CPU/memory scale linearly with attacker size (fixed with a 2048-char cap, matching the module's option 1 + option 3 fix). Key lesson: a clean error log or a flat memory curve is not the end of the investigation -- the profiler must also look at CPU distribution and input-size sensitivity, because resource exhaustion can hide in plain sight. The tool-led discipline paid off: each finding traces back to a specific probe output.
